headline: Applied Materials (AMAT) Q3 FY26 record: rev $9.12B (+25% Y/Y) vs $8.99B est, non-GAAP EPS $3.50 vs $2.71 est (+29% beat); Q4 guide $10.25B ±$500M (+51% Y/Y) crushes $9.55B est; but stock -5% AH on China slipping to 28% of rev (from 35%) plus leading-edge logic timing chatter
summary: Clean beat-and-raise print — AI-driven WFE demand called 'unprecedented,' visibility into another record 2027. Semi Systems accelerating across DRAM, leading-edge foundry-logic, advanced packaging (~80% of WFE growth 2026-2027). Q4 non-GAAP EPS guide $4.02 ±$0.20 up 85% Y/Y. Stock fade in AH tells you the AI equipment complex is priced for perfection — China derisking is medium-term positive but a near-term $ headwind. Read-through positive for LRCX/KLAC/8035.T (Tokyo Electron) on leading-edge etch/deposition strength; supportive for MU/SK Hynix/Samsung on the HBM/DRAM capex signal.

headline: SMIC Q2 2026: revenue tops $3.01B first time (+20% Q/Q), non-GAAP EPS $0.06 vs $0.037 est (+61%); gross margin 25.3%, operating profit $534M, net $479M; foundry raising Q3 wafer prices as utilization hits 93.7% — will begin breaking out AI chip revenue as separate line
summary: China's leading foundry is at capacity. Selective Q1 price hikes stuck, Q3 hikes now being pushed through negotiations. Utilization near max on 8-inch equivalent wafers (~2.9M shipped Q2). Story reinforces the global fab-pricing-power narrative: if the constrained Chinese-domestic foundry is raising prices, TSMC/UMC/GFS pricing discipline holds. Constructive read-across for the WFE names (AMAT / LRCX / KLAC / 8035.T / ASML) on sustained capex through 2027. Hong Kong-listed SMIC +6.4% intraday.

headline: Foxconn (Hon Hai) Q2 2026: net profit NT$59.97B (~$1.86B, +35% Y/Y) beats NT$58.8B est; cloud & networking segment 51% of Q2 revenue (up from 48% Q1) — AI servers exceed iPhones + consumer electronics combined for the first time in company history; AI rack shipments to grow high double-digit % sequentially in Q3, full-year rack shipments forecast to more than double vs 2025
summary: A structural marker for the AI infra chain. Foxconn — the world's largest EMS and Nvidia's primary rack integrator — now derives the majority of revenue from AI/cloud rather than smartphones. Confirms the GB200/GB300 Blackwell ramp is scaling into H2. Positive read-through: NVDA (rack demand), DELL/SMCI/CLS/HPE (competitive tape), VRT/ETN/APH (thermal, power, interconnect content per rack), TSM (CoWoS packaging bottleneck named as the 2027 ceiling by Foxconn CEO).

headline: Cisco (CSCO) collects five analyst PT raises after Q4 FY26 blowout — Truist $125→$140 Buy, UBS $132→$138 Buy, Rosenblatt $150→$165 Buy, Morgan Stanley $130→$135 OW, KeyBanc $130→$135 OW; consensus themes: 'networking supercycle,' FY27 guide seen conservative, AI hyperscaler order book validated
summary: Sell-side follow-through on the $4B Q4 AI order print / $9.3B FY26 AI orders (4.5x FY25). Stock had faded 8.4% post-print on margin guide (65-66% GM below Street) but analysts framing that as buying opportunity given order visibility. Rosenblatt Street-high at $165 (+45% upside). Read-through remains positive for ANET (competing but growing pie), AVGO (Tomahawk ASICs), VRT/APH/CLS on the networking hardware content chain.

headline: Google launches Gemini 3.7 Flash overnight — outperforms predecessor on coding/debugging benchmarks, generates deployable production code first-try, cheaper per-token; Gemini Spark productivity agent moves to 3.7 Flash today. Top-tier Gemini 3.5 Pro release still delayed
summary: Incremental Flash tier upgrade — meaningful for developer tooling economics and for GOOGL's positioning in the coding-agent race against Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex. The Pro tier delay is the more strategic tell: Google's frontier model cadence continues to trail the Anthropic/OpenAI pace. Neutral for GOOGL near-term; watch impact on Vertex AI/Cursor/Windsurf ecosystem economics. Also reduces per-token spend for enterprises running high-volume inference on Google infra.

headline: China tech tape lifts hardware over internet — SMIC +6.4% in Hong Kong on beat + stronger GM guide; Chinese hardware/foundry stocks outperforming platform names; Bloomberg notes rotation reinforces the 'AI hardware supercycle' thesis vs consumer-facing internet
summary: A signal beyond individual print: capital in Asia is rotating from consumer internet (weak recovery) toward semis and hardware (concrete AI demand). Confirms the same rotation seen in US markets (SMCI/CRWV/AVGO leading QQQ). Positive read-through for the Asian hardware chain — 005930.KS (Samsung), 000660.KS (SK Hynix), TSM, 8035.T, 4063.T (Shin-Etsu), ASX, AMKR — into the Aug 25 Hot Chips week where Samsung/SK will detail HBM4 base-die and packaging roadmaps.

headline: S&P 500 and Nasdaq at record highs into Friday open; S&P futures +0.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.3% after cool July CPI (3.4%/2.5%) + benign PPI Thursday; September Fed hike odds have fallen sharply, MSCI ACWI also at record; SanDisk +6% pre-market on OpenAI IPO watch
summary: Third straight weekly advance for global equities. Softer inflation + weaker payrolls have collapsed the September hike premium, extending the AI risk-on trade. Powell's Jackson Hole speech next Friday (Aug 22) is the next macro pivot — dovish tone would confirm the September pause narrative and add fuel to the AI/hyperscaler beta trade. Watch OpenAI IPO tape as it firms up ($40B+ revenue run rate reported Thursday); positive-adjacent for SanDisk, NVDA, MSFT (large stakeholder), Oracle, CRWV as OpenAI ecosystem infra beneficiaries.
